doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Her WBAI radio show 'A Delicate Balance'
summary: During a fallow period she approached Chris Albertson at WBAI and hosted an unpaid jazz show with guests like Benny Goodman, Herbie Hancock and Bill Evans, most tapes now lost.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: . . . to try to juggle that with being a performer, being a producer and entrepreneur. I think at that time you also had an early radio program that you had delved in at certain points. Am I correct?

Yes, you are correct. What I did was, during this fallow period, it seemed like other people . . . that I was not getting recorded. I felt bad about it. So having this time when I really wasn’t working all the time, I called up a guy at . . . now I can’t think of the radio station. The Pacifica station. WBAI. Chris Albertson was working there. I called up Chris and said, “I’d like to come up there and play some records, do an hour or two of jazz, because I don’t hear enough in New York.” I knew I wasn’t going to get paid. I would go up there with a bundle of records. I called the show “A Delicate Balance.” I had guests like Benny Goodman and Herbie and Bill Evans. It’s really terrible. I think all those tapes . . . I did not take care of keeping those tapes. I only have some of them. I have one that I did with Alec Wilder and one that I did with Jimmy and George Wettling, but I can’t find the one with Herbie or . . . So anyway, that got me off my ass, so to speak, dealing with radio and talking to people.
Yes, o.k., so that probably right now brings us up to around the mid-’70s of your career.
